slides.headline: Long drive, stiff mid-back?
slides.sub: Simple changes for the car, and what to do when you get out.

slides.title: Why long drives stiffen you up
slides.body: Hours in one position, a fixed arm reach and road vibration can leave the mid-back feeling stiff and achy. It's usually about staying still for too long, not damage to your spine.

slides.title: Set up the seat first
slides.body: Sit back fully in the seat, bring it close enough that your elbows stay softly bent, and tilt the backrest slightly back from upright. A small rolled towel behind your lower back can help.

slides.title: Break it up every two hours
slides.body: Road safety advice already suggests a break every two hours. Use it well: walk for a few minutes, reach your arms overhead, squeeze your shoulder blades back and gently rotate each way.

slides.title: Where chiropractic care fits
slides.body: If stiffness keeps coming back, our chiropractors can assess your mid-back and neck, use adjustments or soft tissue work where appropriate, and give you mobility exercises to use between drives.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: See a doctor promptly if mid-back pain comes with chest pain, shortness of breath, fever or unexplained weight loss, follows a crash or fall, or is constant and worse at night.

slides.headline: Stiff after every road trip?
slides.body: Book with our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy. We'll assess what's going on, use hands-on care where it helps and send you off with a few simple exercises.

caption:
Hours behind the wheel and your mid-back feels like a plank of wood?

Long drives keep you in one position with a fixed reach and constant vibration. The stiffness that follows is usually about stillness, not damage. Start with your seat: sit right back, elbows softly bent, backrest tilted slightly back, and a rolled towel behind your lower back if it helps.

Then use the two-hourly break road safety advice already recommends. Walk for a few minutes, reach overhead, squeeze your shoulder blades back and gently rotate each way.

If it keeps coming back, our chiropractors can assess your mid-back and neck and pair hands-on care with simple mobility work. See a doctor promptly if pain comes with chest pain, breathlessness or fever.
